o.text:
From Proto-Turkic *kalï- (“to rise”)
Cognates
Cognate with Old Uyghur [script needed] (kalı-, “to rise in the air”), Karakhanid [script needed] (kalɨ̄māk, “to buck, jump”), Turkish kalkmak (“to rise, ascend, get up”), Bashkir ҡалҡыу (qalqıw, “to rise”), Kazakh қалқу (qalquw, “to soar”), Kyrgyz калкуу (kalkuu, “to float”), Southern Altai калыыр (kalïïr, “to jump, hop”), Tatar калку (qalqu, “to rise”), Turkmen galkmak (“to rise”), Tuvan халыыр (xalıır, “to jump, run”), Uzbek qalqmoq (“to rise, swell, jump”), Yakut кылый (kïlïy, “to hop along”).
Borrowed from Arabic رِيَاضِيَّات pl (riyāḍiyyāt). By surface analysis, riyaz + -iyyat.
Calque of Russian общеупотреби́тельный (obščeupotrebítelʹnyj). By surface analysis, ümum- + işlək.
Borrowed from Russian методология (metodologija). By surface analysis, metod + -logiya.
